paragraphs: Federated learning produces a shared model from data held by different clients, but a new client's data can differ from the training distributions. This paper studies personalization at test time without labeled examples. The goal is for clients to adapt the shared model locally using only their available unlabeled data.

The authors argue that existing test-time adaptation methods often overlook the relationships between the multiple source distributions in federated learning. Many also decide in advance which model components can change. Their proposed method, ATP, instead learns adaptation rates for individual components from distribution differences among training clients. This makes the amount of adjustment something learned from experience with shifts.

The paper provides a theoretical generalization analysis and reports experiments involving changes in label distributions, corrupted images, and domain shifts. ATP outperforms the tested adaptation methods across multiple datasets and architectures. These findings support learning how different components should adapt when personalization must work without test-time labels.
neurips-2023-adaptive-test-time-personal.tldr: ATP learns how strongly to adapt each model component so federated clients can personalize a shared model without test-time labels.

paragraphs: A reinforcement learning system can satisfy an average cost limit while still incurring an unacceptable cost during a particular episode. This paper studies a stronger requirement: maintain a cost bound at every round of every episode, measured against a reference policy called a policy prior, while optimizing expected reward.

The authors formalize this requirement as an Anytime-Competitive Markov Decision Process and introduce the ACRL algorithm. Its central guarantee concerns costs throughout an episode, so compliance does not depend solely on averaging over random outcomes. The policy prior supplies the comparison used by the competitive constraint.

The paper proves that ACRL satisfies these anytime constraints. Its regret analysis also shows that the learned policy asymptotically reaches the best reward achievable under those constraints. This comparison is specifically with the constrained optimum, rather than an unrestricted reward maximum. Experiments in carbon-intelligent computing support both the algorithm's reward performance and its cost guarantees, connecting the formal objective to an application where costs matter during operation.
neurips-2023-anytime-competitive-reinfor.tldr: ACRL learns to maximize reward while provably respecting cost constraints at every round relative to a reference policy.

paragraphs: Neural methods can learn to construct solutions to combinatorial optimization problems, but transferring that ability to unfamiliar problem sizes remains difficult. This paper changes the decision-making representation used for learning. It starts with a Markov decision process in which successive choices build a solution, then reduces its state space using bisimulation quotienting.

This reduction groups states that are equivalent for the relevant decision process. For problems with recursive structure, the authors specialize the construction to exploit problem symmetries. They prove that an optimal policy in the reduced process solves the associated optimization problem, establishing that the representation preserves the desired solution objective.

The approach is evaluated on two traveling salesman variants, vehicle routing, orienteering, and knapsack. Simple attention-based policies learn by imitating optimal or near-optimal solutions to small instances from one distribution. The authors report state-of-the-art results on synthetic and realistic benchmarks, including strong transfer to much larger instances without additional search. The theoretical result concerns optimal policies; the reported generalization concerns the learned policies in these experiments.
neurips-2023-bq-nco-bisimulation-quotien.tldr: BQ-NCO uses problem symmetries to simplify sequential optimization and learns policies that generalize well to larger tested instances.

paragraphs: Neural decoding connects recorded brain activity with behavior. Many methods first assign each detected electrical spike to an individual neuron, a step called spike sorting. Incorrect assignments and poorly represented uncertainty can discard useful information before decoding even begins. Dense recording probes now provide rich spike features that allow a different approach.

The proposed method models these features directly with a mixture of Gaussian distributions. It represents uncertainty about spike assignments without explicitly solving the problem of clustering spikes into neurons. The mixture proportions change over time in response to behavior, linking changes in the feature distribution to the behavioral signal being decoded.

The authors develop variational inference procedures both to fit this model and to decode behavior. Across recordings from different animals and probe geometries, their decoder consistently outperforms the tested threshold-based and spike-sorting-based methods. The findings support retaining uncertainty in the decoding model and using information available in unsorted recordings, rather than requiring a separate neuron-assignment stage before behavioral prediction.
neurips-2023-bypassing-spike-sorting-den.tldr: A density-based neural decoder models unsorted spike features and assignment uncertainty to improve behavioral decoding in the reported recordings.

paragraphs: Finding an object in a city-scale 3D scene from a written description requires connecting language with geometry, appearance, and location. Point clouds capture detailed outdoor structures, but the shortage of accompanying text makes this task difficult to study. CityRefer supplies annotations for grounding descriptions in specific objects within urban scenes.

The dataset contains 35,000 natural-language descriptions of objects in SensatUrban scenes and 5,000 landmark labels aligned with OpenStreetMap. All descriptions and labels were manually checked. Combining object descriptions with geographic landmarks provides information beyond the shape and appearance of isolated objects, making city geography part of the grounding task.

The authors also develop a baseline system that learns from language, 3D object instances, and landmark geography. This establishes a way to evaluate models using the dataset's complementary information sources. They describe CityRefer as the largest dataset of its kind to their knowledge. Its contribution is infrastructure for studying city-level object localization, with potential applications in language-guided interaction with autonomous vehicles and drones.
neurips-2023-cityrefer-geography-aware-3.tldr: CityRefer links urban 3D objects with verified language descriptions and geographic landmarks to support city-scale visual grounding.

paragraphs: In a contextual bandit problem, a learner sees a context, chooses an action, and observes a reward. This paper assumes that the S contexts can be grouped into r categories: within each category, every action has the same expected reward across contexts. The number of groups is at most the smaller of S and the number of actions, K.

Under this assumption, the authors give an algorithm that finds a policy within epsilon of optimal using roughly r(S + K)/epsilon² samples, with high probability and logarithmic factors suppressed. They prove a matching lower bound at that level of precision. This establishes nearly optimal data requirements for learning a good policy when the shared reward structure exists.

For learning while accumulating rewards, they provide a cumulative regret bound of roughly the square root of r³(S + K)T over T rounds, again suppressing logarithmic factors. They also extend their algorithms to more general low-rank bandits, improving regret bounds in some scenarios. The gains therefore depend on exploitable structure in how contexts and actions determine rewards.
neurips-2023-context-lumpable-stochastic.tldr: When contexts share action-reward profiles in groups, bandit algorithms can achieve nearly optimal sample requirements by exploiting that structure.

paragraphs: Federated learning becomes particularly challenging when clients have different local data distributions and the combined population contains many examples of some classes but few of others. Local observations alone can make the overall imbalance difficult to characterize. Privacy constraints also complicate adapting methods that assume all training data are available centrally.

Fed-GraB connects two modules in a feedback loop. A Direct Prior Analyzer evaluates the global long-tailed distribution, and a Self-adjusting Gradient Balancer uses that feedback to reweight clients' gradients. The balancing process therefore responds to the estimated global imbalance while influencing the updates made during local learning.

The authors report that this approach reduces distribution drift arising from client heterogeneity and improves the global model's minority-class performance while maintaining majority-class performance. Experiments achieve state-of-the-art results on CIFAR-10-LT, CIFAR-100-LT, ImageNet-LT, and iNaturalist. These findings support coordinating local gradient adjustments with information about the overall class distribution, rather than treating client differences and rare classes as independent training problems.
neurips-2023-fed-grab-federated-long-tai.tldr: Fed-GraB uses feedback about global class imbalance to adjust federated gradients and improve minority-class performance.

paragraphs: Detecting generated images requires evaluation data that reflect the variety of images and generators a detector may encounter. GenImage addresses a shortage of large datasets containing outputs from advanced image-generation systems. It includes more than one million pairs of generated and collected real images, spanning many image classes.

The generated portion includes outputs from diffusion models and generative adversarial networks. Beyond assembling the data, the authors define two evaluation tasks. Cross-generator classification trains a detector on one generator and tests it on others, examining whether its learned distinctions transfer beyond the source used for training.

The second task evaluates detection after image degradation, including reduced resolution, blur, and compression. Together, these tasks assess two different demands: recognizing outputs from other generators and handling changes to image quality. The paper contributes a large, varied dataset and an evaluation framework for developing and comparing detectors under conditions intended to resemble practical use. Its stated value lies in enabling more thorough assessment across image content, generator families, and degradation conditions.
neurips-2023-genimage-a-million-scale-be.tldr: GenImage provides a million-scale dataset and tests for evaluating generated-image detectors across generators and degraded image conditions.

paragraphs: Knowledge graph embedding models assign scores to possible relationships between entities, making them useful for predicting missing links. This paper examines CP, RESCAL, TuckER, and ComplEx. Interpreting these models as energy-based systems creates difficulties for exact maximum-likelihood learning, sampling new relationships, and enforcing logical constraints.

The authors reinterpret their scoring functions as computational circuits with structural restrictions that permit efficient marginalization. They then provide two ways to construct generative models: constrain activations to be nonnegative or square the circuit outputs. These transformations connect familiar link-prediction models to a framework that supports additional probabilistic operations.

The resulting models support exact maximum-likelihood learning, efficient generation of new triples, and logical constraints that hold by construction. The authors report little or no loss in link-prediction performance and more favorable scaling on graphs containing millions of entities. The contribution is therefore a change in model formulation that expands what knowledge graph embeddings can do while largely preserving their demonstrated predictive usefulness.
neurips-2023-how-to-turn-your-knowledge-.tldr: Recasting knowledge graph embeddings as probabilistic circuits enables exact learning, efficient generation, and logical constraints with little or no predictive loss.

paragraphs: Active human involvement lets a person interrupt an agent during training and demonstrate a preferred action. This paper introduces Proxy Value Propagation, a method that turns those interventions into a learning signal without requiring a reward function. Its aim is to use corrective interaction to train policies that emulate human behavior.

The method assigns high proxy values to state-action pairs demonstrated by the person and low values to agent actions that prompted intervention. It then uses temporal-difference learning to propagate these labeled values to other, unlabeled experience collected during exploration. Human feedback can consequently influence decisions beyond the exact examples where an intervention occurred.

Human-in-the-loop experiments demonstrate learning across both continuous and discrete control tasks using different human control devices. The tested tasks include driving in Grand Theft Auto V, and the method requires only small changes to existing reinforcement learning algorithms. These results support the usefulness of a proxy value function as a practical bridge between sparse corrective demonstrations and policy optimization across a broader set of agent experiences.
neurips-2023-learning-from-active-human-.tldr: Proxy Value Propagation trains agents without a reward function by spreading value signals from human demonstrations and interventions.

paragraphs: Linker design seeks a molecular connection between fragments that together form a stable candidate molecule. This is a challenging part of targeted protein degradation approaches such as PROTACs. Existing models assume that the fragments' relative positions are already known, even though that information may be unavailable in practical design settings.

LinkerNet tackles the joint problem of placing the fragments and generating the linker's three-dimensional structure. It uses a 3D equivariant diffusion model to learn both processes together. The model treats each fragment as a rigid body, and its pose-prediction module draws inspiration from the Newton-Euler equations used in rigid-body mechanics.

Experiments on ZINC and PROTAC-DB show that the method can generate molecules with chemical validity, synthetic accessibility, and low energy in both constrained and unconstrained settings. These findings support treating fragment arrangement and linker structure as coupled design choices. The demonstrated contribution is molecular generation under this broader setup, including cases where fragment poses are not supplied in advance.
neurips-2023-linkernet-fragment-poses-an.tldr: LinkerNet jointly generates molecular linkers and fragment poses, allowing linker design when relative fragment positions are unknown.

paragraphs: Machine learning for materials discovery needs access to varied tasks, suitable data, and comparable evaluations. The authors identify the lack of an integrated platform as one reason this area has progressed more slowly than molecular modeling for drug discovery. M²Hub brings these resources together in a toolkit spanning the materials discovery workflow.

Its first release covers virtual screening, inverse design, and molecular simulation. It contains nine datasets representing six types of materials, with 56 tasks across eight categories of material properties. Two additional synthetic datasets support generative tasks. This breadth allows researchers to explore several stages of discovery through a shared collection of resources.

The toolkit also supplies three data partitions beyond random splitting, intended to reflect practical materials discovery scenarios. The authors benchmark leading machine learning methods on representative tasks, including approaches suitable for materials structures that had not previously been compared in the literature. The contribution is an integrated experimental foundation: datasets, methods, evaluation choices, and benchmark results that make materials-focused machine learning easier to investigate systematically.
neurips-2023-m-2-hub-unlocking-the-poten.tldr: M²Hub integrates datasets, tasks, methods, and benchmarks for machine learning across major stages of materials discovery.

paragraphs: Studying environmental conditions alongside public health requires data aligned across places and time. MedSat addresses this need by combining environmental, sociodemographic, satellite, and prescription indicators for every Lower Layer Super Output Area in England. Its coverage includes 2019 and 2020, providing data from before and during COVID.

The dataset contains 111 sociodemographic features, 43 environmental point features such as greenery and air pollution, and four seasonal satellite composites with 11 bands each. Prescription measures cover depression, anxiety, diabetes, hypertension, asthma, opioids, and total prescriptions. Bringing these sources together makes different aspects of local environmental and health context available within one dataset.

The authors present MedSat as an opportunity for new public-health machine learning methods. They identify challenges involving complex data, feature engineering, spatial and temporal relationships, imbalance, explainability, and geographic generalization. Satellite-based health modeling is another proposed direction. The paper's contribution is the integrated data resource that enables these investigations, rather than a reported causal finding about environmental exposure or a demonstrated health-prediction method.
neurips-2023-medsat-a-public-health-data.tldr: MedSat combines England-wide prescription, environmental, sociodemographic, and satellite data to support public-health machine learning.

paragraphs: Regular expressions encode expert knowledge for networking tasks such as intrusion detection, but they cannot directly improve from labeled examples. Neural networks can learn from data, yet they can struggle before enough examples are available and may be too costly for network devices. Metis connects these complementary capabilities in a staged framework.

First, Metis converts regular expressions into byte-level recurrent neural networks without training. These networks retain the expert knowledge needed for cold-start operation and can subsequently improve through training when labeled data become available. A semi-supervised knowledge-distillation step then transforms them into pooling soft random forests suitable for deployment on network devices.

The authors evaluate the framework using three weeks of traffic collected on their campus. They report higher accuracy than the original regular expressions and other tested baselines, together with superior throughput on network devices. The results support a path from existing expert rules to trainable models and then to deployable inference systems, combining an immediate starting point with the ability to improve from data.
neurips-2023-metis-understanding-and-enh.tldr: Metis converts regular expressions into trainable neural models and distills them into models deployable on network devices.

paragraphs: Mnemosyne is a learned optimizer: a model trained to update another neural network's parameters. The paper uses Transformers with a low-rank implicit attention mechanism operating across parameters and training time. The aim is to train entire networks, including other Transformers, without tuning the optimizer separately for each task.

The authors report that Mnemosyne outperforms LSTM-based learned optimizers, including versions with additional features intended to reduce forgetting. It also matches the accuracy achieved by leading hand-designed optimizers with carefully tuned hyperparameters, often producing the best-performing models. Its meta-training uses simple strategies described as requiring minimal computational resources.

The evaluation covers Vision Transformer fine-tuning, BERT pretraining, and soft prompt tuning of T5XXL models with more than 11 billion parameters. Mnemosyne's memory complexity is comparable to hand-designed first-order optimizers, which supports scaling to larger parameter sets. The paper also analyzes its compact associative memory theoretically. Together, these contributions address both the effectiveness of learned update rules and the memory requirements that determine where such optimizers can be used.
neurips-2023-mnemosyne-learning-to-train.tldr: Mnemosyne uses Transformers as learned optimizers, matching carefully tuned conventional optimizers in reported accuracy while retaining comparable memory complexity.

paragraphs: Monarch Mixer explores whether models can maintain strong performance while scaling less than quadratically with both sequence length and model width. Its common building block is the Monarch matrix, a structured matrix class that supports expressive linear transformations and efficient GPU computation. The architecture uses this primitive along both dimensions.

The paper tests the idea in BERT-style language modeling, image classification, and GPT-style language modeling. In the reported BERT comparisons, it matches downstream GLUE quality with up to 27% fewer parameters and reaches up to 9.1 times the throughput at sequence length 4K. On ImageNet, it exceeds ViT-b accuracy by 1% with half the parameters.

Causal language modeling requires preventing access to future tokens, but ordinary masking creates a quadratic bottleneck. The authors develop a parameterization based on multivariate polynomial evaluation and interpolation that preserves causality and subquadratic scaling. At 360 million parameters, the resulting model matches GPT-style Transformers in pretraining perplexity on The PILE. These proof-of-concept results suggest that Transformer-level quality may be possible without attention or MLPs.
neurips-2023-monarch-mixer-a-simple-sub-.tldr: Monarch Mixer uses structured matrices to achieve subquadratic scaling and competitive Transformer quality in language and vision experiments.

paragraphs: A neural functional takes another neural network's weights as input. This is useful when a network itself represents data, but its weight space can be large and contain symmetries. Reordering interchangeable internal units changes the weight arrangement without changing the represented function, so a model processing those weights should respect that structure.

Neural Functional Transformers introduce attention-based layers that are equivariant to weight-space permutations. Their outputs transform consistently with those permutations, allowing the layers to be stacked into deep models while preserving the symmetry. Experiments on feedforward MLP and CNN weights show performance matching or exceeding earlier weight-space methods.

The authors also use these models to construct Inr2Array, which maps the weights of implicit neural representations into permutation-invariant latent representations. Here, the final representation stays unchanged under the relevant weight permutations. The method improves classification accuracy for implicit neural representations by up to 17% over existing approaches. The results support attention as a useful building block for learning from networks while accounting for the symmetries of their parameters.
neurips-2023-neural-functional-transform.tldr: Neural Functional Transformers apply symmetry-respecting attention to neural network weights, improving several weight-processing tasks.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to generate a new sample resembling an unknown distribution while protecting the privacy of the dataset used to produce it. The input consists of independent samples drawn from that distribution. The target is a sampling distribution close to the original in total variation distance, subject to differential privacy.

The authors develop algorithms for multidimensional Gaussian distributions under three information settings: known covariance, unknown but bounded covariance, and unknown unbounded covariance. Covariance describes how the coordinates vary together. The distinction matters because the available information changes what the private sampling procedure must accomplish from the observed data.

The paper establishes nearly optimal sample complexity for the known-covariance and unknown-bounded-covariance settings. It also studies product distributions over binary vectors and gives a pure differential privacy algorithm where an approximate differential privacy algorithm had previously been known, with slightly worse sample complexity. These results sharpen both the data requirements and privacy guarantees available for sampling from the specified distribution families.
neurips-2023-on-differentially-private-s.tldr: New private sampling algorithms improve guarantees for Gaussian and binary product distributions, with nearly optimal data requirements in two Gaussian settings.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning trains a policy from existing data, which is useful when further exploration is infeasible. Two concerns arise: the policy may choose actions poorly supported by the dataset, and it may accept actions with dangerous random outcomes. This paper proposes addressing both through one risk-sensitive decision-making mechanism.

The method, 1R2R, uses an ensemble of environment models to estimate epistemic uncertainty, meaning uncertainty from limited knowledge. It also accounts for aleatoric uncertainty, meaning randomness in the environment. A risk-averse policy avoids actions with high uncertainty, whether that uncertainty reflects insufficient data or genuinely variable outcomes.

Within this approach, aversion to epistemic uncertainty discourages leaving regions covered by the dataset, while aversion to aleatoric uncertainty discourages environmentally risky actions. Experiments show strong performance on deterministic benchmarks and better performance than existing approaches on risk-sensitive objectives in stochastic domains. The findings support treating uncertainty about the model and randomness within the modeled environment through a shared risk objective when learning policies from fixed data.
neurips-2023-one-risk-to-rule-them-all-a.tldr: 1R2R uses risk aversion to address both poorly supported actions and risky environmental randomness in offline reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Protein generation benefits from learning across many families while remaining steerable toward a particular family. Existing approaches can struggle with that steering or require training on a large alignment from the target family. PoET addresses this tension by learning a generative model of entire protein families across tens of millions of natural sequence clusters.

It represents a family as a sequence of protein sequences. Within each protein, tokens are modeled sequentially; between proteins, attention is invariant to their order. This architecture allows the model to use contexts longer than those encountered during training. Retrieved family sequences can condition generation and scoring of modifications, including for small families.

On deep mutational scanning datasets, PoET outperforms the tested protein language models and evolutionary sequence models at predicting variant function across proteins with different alignment depths. The authors also demonstrate controlled generation of new protein sequences. The results support combining cross-family learning with family-specific context, allowing one model to use broad sequence experience while responding to the family supplied at use time.
neurips-2023-poet-a-generative-model-of-.tldr: PoET learns across protein families while using retrieved family sequences to guide protein generation and variant-function prediction.

paragraphs: Generating a sample from a diffusion model involves solving a differential equation, which can require many expensive model evaluations. Many fast samplers use deterministic ordinary differential equations because of their efficiency. This paper investigates efficient stochastic sampling, motivated by the possibility that randomness can offer additional advantages for sample quality and diversity.

The authors analyze variance-controlled stochastic diffusion equations and linear multistep solvers. From this analysis, they develop SA-Solver, an improved stochastic Adams method. Its multistep formulation uses information across solver steps to support efficient generation while retaining a stochastic sampling process.

Experiments show improved or comparable performance against leading samplers when only a few sampling steps are used. With a suitable number of function evaluations, SA-Solver also achieves state-of-the-art FID on the reported benchmark datasets. That evaluation budget is part of the stated result. The work therefore supports stochastic equation solving as a competitive route to fast diffusion sampling, with the reported quality gains tied to the tested sampling regimes.
neurips-2023-sa-solver-stochastic-adams-.tldr: SA-Solver accelerates stochastic diffusion sampling and achieves competitive few-step performance and leading FID at suitable evaluation budgets.

paragraphs: Predicting several people's movements requires accounting for how they react to and anticipate one another. This paper studies that problem in settings with strategic interaction. It introduces Wusi, a 3D multi-person motion dataset based on team sports, where intense interactions and varied poses provide material for studying socially coordinated movement.

The authors formulate motion prediction from a multi-agent reinforcement learning perspective. They combine behavioral cloning with generative adversarial imitation learning to improve learning efficiency and generalization. Both use observed behavior to support learning, placing the prediction task within a framework that models multiple interacting decision-makers.

The method also introduces a cognitive hierarchy framework inspired by the human process of planning social actions. Its purpose is to predict strategic interactions rather than considering each person's movement in isolation. Comprehensive experiments support the effectiveness of the dataset and approach. The contribution combines a benchmark, a learning formulation, and a cognition-inspired modeling framework, making strategic multi-person movement the common focus of both the data and the prediction method.
neurips-2023-social-motion-prediction-wi.tldr: The paper combines a team-sports motion dataset with imitation learning and cognitive hierarchies to predict strategic human interactions.

paragraphs: Many language tasks involve judging the relationship between two texts rather than generating a continuation. This paper proposes text alignment as a shared formulation for entailment, similarity, question answering, answerability, and factual consistency. The model measures how closely the information in a pair of texts aligns.

The authors fine-tune a 355-million-parameter RoBERTa model using 5.9 million examples from 28 datasets. Across more than 20 evaluation datasets, the unified model matches or exceeds FLAN-T5 models with roughly two or ten times as many parameters. It also outperforms models fine-tuned separately on individual task datasets.

On factual-consistency evaluation across 23 datasets, it improves over several baselines, including GPT-3.5 and sometimes GPT-4. As an add-on to language models for question answering, identifying unanswerable questions improves average exact match by 17.94 and F1 by 15.05 in the reported experiments. The findings show that a less versatile but broadly shared comparison task can support strong performance with a much smaller model.
neurips-2023-text-alignment-is-an-effici.tldr: A compact text-alignment model handles diverse language-evaluation tasks and often matches or exceeds much larger models in reported comparisons.

paragraphs: Studying compressible turbulent flows requires detailed three-dimensional data, but high-fidelity simulation datasets are limited. BLASTNet 2.0 provides a 2.2-terabyte collection containing 744 full-domain samples from 34 direct numerical simulations. It covers both reacting and non-reacting flows, supporting research on physical systems relevant to propulsion, energy, and the environment.

The authors use this collection to benchmark 49 variants of five deep learning approaches for 3D super-resolution, which aims to recover finer spatial detail. Their scaling analysis examines how predictive performance changes with model size and computational cost. The comparison includes two scientific machine learning techniques.

Three findings emerge: predictive performance can improve with scale, architecture choices matter substantially for smaller models, and benefits from physics-based losses can persist as models grow. These observations make size only one consideration in designing a super-resolution model. The benchmark provides evidence about architecture and training objectives alongside a public data resource expected to support broader machine learning research in flow physics.
neurips-2023-turbulence-in-focus-benchma.tldr: BLASTNet 2.0 benchmarks 3D turbulence super-resolution, showing how model scale, architecture, and physics-based losses affect performance.

paragraphs: Privately estimating quantiles becomes challenging when the data range is not known in advance, especially near the maximum. This paper develops a method that works without an upper bound by using AboveThreshold, a subroutine associated with the Sparse Vector Technique. Two invocations extend the approach to data unbounded in both directions.

The authors also refine the privacy analysis of AboveThreshold, giving a more general characterization of its privacy loss. This improves guarantees for their estimator and for the widely used Sparse Vector Technique. Computationally, the algorithm needs one linear-time pass through potentially unsorted data, after which each subsequent query takes constant time.

Experiments compare the unbounded method with leading algorithms designed for bounded data. It often performs better for interior quantiles on nonsynthetic datasets and performs significantly better for maximal quantiles used in private sum computation. High-quantile estimation is useful here because it supports choosing clipping levels for private sums and means. The contribution connects handling unknown ranges with improved privacy analysis and practical estimation accuracy.
neurips-2023-unbounded-differentially-pr.tldr: An AboveThreshold-based method privately estimates quantiles without known range bounds and improves high-quantile estimation in reported experiments.
